definition: The suprasegmental qualities of speech: pitch contour, loudness, rhythm, and phrasing.
details: The suprasegmental qualities of speech: pitch contour, loudness, rhythm, and phrasing. Prosody is where "correct but robotic" TTS fails; controllable-prosody models expose these as knobs, and Arabic prosody interacts with diacritization and dialect.

explainer.lead: The suprasegmental qualities of speech: pitch contour, loudness, rhythm, and phrasing. It is where correct but robotic text-to-speech fails.

tiers.eli5: It is the melody of speech — the rises, falls, and rhythm that make talking sound alive rather than flat.
tiers.practitioner: Controllable-prosody models expose these qualities as adjustable knobs. A pitfall noted in the details is that Arabic prosody interacts with diacritization and dialect.
tiers.paperLevel: Defined as suprasegmental qualities — pitch contour, loudness, rhythm, and phrasing; controllable-prosody models expose them as knobs, and no formal formula is given.

explainer.example: A text-to-speech system adjusts pitch contour and rhythm so a sentence sounds natural rather than robotic.
